question: If the mind were all-pervading or eternal, would it produce simultaneous or perpetual cognition of everything?
premises: An all-pervading mind would be in contact with all objects at once.
An eternal mind would be constantly available for cognition.
Ordinary experience does not show simultaneous or perpetual cognition of all things.
inference: The hypotheses of an all-pervading or eternal mind entail impossible cognitive consequences.
plain_english: If the mind were all-pervading, there would be simultaneous cognition of everything; and if the mind were eternal, knowledge would arise always.
